meta.title: beautifulnodejs Services — Feature Slices
meta.subtitle: The hexagon with its contract gates on the rings: eslint no-restricted-imports, the proven-fire harness, and the contracts tests make the walls red before review

boundaries.label: Zero-I/O wall: adapters own pg · BullMQ — the domain imports none

cards.title: Vertical slices
items: src/features/<slice>/ ships the same eight files every time: domain.ts · ports.ts · usecase.ts · http.ts · postgres.ts · queries.ts · usecase.test.ts · module.ts
a port is defined where it is consumed — the use case writes ports.ts; no consumer, no port
slices never import each other: shared capability is duplicated through a port or promoted into #shared/platform

cards.title: tsyringe + composition root
items: one root: bin/api.ts + bin/worker.ts build concrete adapters, register them under injection tokens, validate config once
register*(app, Deps) is each slice's whole wiring contract — no container.resolve() inside slices
the domain is I/O-free (no fastify/zod/tsyringe/drizzle/pg/bullmq/pino) — eslint no-restricted-imports makes it red before review

cards.title: The contract gates (machine-enforced)
items: eslint no-restricted-imports groups on every ring above: group 1 the domain is I/O-free · group 2 slices never import #features/* · group 3 use cases touch ports + domain only — behind tsconfig strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess
lints/check proves the gates fire: scripts/check-lints.sh shows all 38 pinned rules red on their marked line, with clean.ts staying quiet
CI 'tests' runs tests/contracts/ — a deleted lint or a muted gate (eslint-disable / @ts-expect-error) fails the build, so the contracts ship unbreakable and non-waivable

cards.title: Realtime + queues
items: platform/realtime keeps in-process rooms user:<id>; the Redis adapter is the documented >1-replica evolution of the same port
durable work rides BullMQ: the outbox row in the same DB transaction is what must not be lost — Redis only holds the queue
consumers are idempotent, keyed on a job id, with capped exponential retries and a dead-letter queue
